featured_reviews.name: Christopher Nadar
featured_reviews.review_text: This is a shelter home for children from difficult backgrounds, particularly orphans, runaway boys and street boys. The institution is under the care of the Salesians of Don Bosco (priests and brothers) who reside there and nurture the kids 24*7. There are many volunteers particularly from colleges nearby who volunteer to teach the young boys and train them with skills needed for being successful in their future. There are staff members and the priests and brothers who are always with the kids and the top priority is education of the kids. The institution was established in the year 1987 and from then has many success stories and repatriation stories to the credit of this institution. It is a registered home for children in need of care and protection and is also periodically assessed to function efficiently. You can contribute in kind or can go there and help them as per their present requirements. It's a blessing and an heart touching experience to spend time with these kids, express our love for them and care for them, They haven't got it enough. WELCOME to Shelter Don Bosco. Moreover pray for this institution and everyone there. The boys are in the age group of 10-18 yrs of age.

featured_reviews.name: Eknath Chandrakant Pawar
featured_reviews.review_text:
ABOUT PRAJA

Praja is a non-partisan organisation working towards enabling accountable governance since 1999. Praja empowers citizens to participate in governance by providing knowledge and perspective so that they can become politically active and involved beyond the ballot box. It undertakes extensive research and highlights civic issues to build the awareness of, and mobilize action by the government and elected representatives (ERs).

THE PROBLEM

Praja believes that uninformed and disengaged ERs and administration, rather than existing systems or policies, are responsible for the lack of good governance. There is a paucity of tools to facilitate effective interaction between citizens and the local government.

PRAJA's RESPONSE

Praja conducts data driven research and provides information on civic issues to citizens, media, and government administration and works with ERs to identify and address inefficiencies in their work processes, bridge the information gaps, and help them in taking corrective measures.

HOW DID IT EVOLVE?

1999: Praja, along with the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC), created Mumbai's first Citizen Charter
2003: Teamed up with BMC and built its citizens' grievance redressal mechanism, the Online Complaint and Management System (OCMS), and conducted complaint audits in the ensuing years
2005: Published Mumbai Citizen's Handbook to demystify governance in Mumbai; About 2 lakh copies distributed
2008: Initiated Praja Dialogue; launched CityScan, an online collation of extensive data on civic and security Issues In Mumbai; Published councillor handbook; and annual report cards on MLAs, and councillors
2014: Conducted workshops with ERs, educating them on policies and roles; started the Delhi Chapter to replicate the model developed In Mumbai
2016: Launched MLA and Councillor Report Cards in Delhi

He was so rude if the doctors are rude to the relatives n our young children who would want to take our responsibilities. This is to inform you I have stopped going to take my ART medicines n if anything happens to me I'll hold this doctor responsible. He takes heavy package of salary just to write the dosage. He doesn't check patients BP, pulse he makes the patient stand at the door of his cabin. He never ask his patients to sit. If he is so scared of HIV infection he should not be in this field. Both my legs are totally damaged even then I climbed the steps as he was not giving months medicine. My daughter is a teacher with the final exams n results on she cannot take leave every now n then n I cannot travel because of weak legs. I want immediate action to be taken against the doctor as I have not collected my ART medicines. I have been a peer councillor at ARCON and well aware of the protocol that a doctor has to follow while checking a patient. This doctor does nothing except for writing in the file which can be done by the admin too. At L&T the blood pressure is checked by a receptionist not even a proper nurse. I know identity of the patient may be the protocol but what if I say it is the place where I live and I don't want to be identified as a positive patient n I don't want my photo in the book. I don't think you can force me. I hope the concerned official take some action. I am totally unfit to travel  because of my age n also because of multiple accidents my both legs are useless. I am also a hypertension n a diabetic patient with denervation problem of my leg due to my illness. Hope you respond to my male. name: Kherwadi Social Welfare Association
description: Kherwadi Social Welfare Association (KSWA) was founded in 1928 by Late Shri. B.G. Kher, a freedom fighter, statesman and the first Premier of Bombay State. He was moved by the plight and miserable living conditions of the 100 odd tanner families who had settled in the marshes of Bandra (E). While he was involved in the freedom struggle, leading two ministries in 1937 and 1946, interspersed with prison terms, his friends and associates started the Chamdewalla-ki-wadi in 1928 and continued to work in the area, which later came to be known as "Kherwadi".

name: Society for Nutrition, Education and Health Action (SNEHA)
description:
Society for Nutrition, Education and Health Action (SNEHA) is a registered non-governmental organization (NGO), established in 1999, to work on the health of women and children in urban vulnerable settlements.
We work on preventive and promotive healthcare to improve metrics of health, nutrition and safety of women, adolescents and children living in the most vulnerable urban informal settlements.

SNEHA strives to build evidence based models of urban health, which can then be replicated in other regions, across four major public health areas - maternal and newborn health, child health and nutrition, adolescent health and gender-based violence.
